messages:
elaine: Dropped a fresh set of comps for the streaming chat UI. Two interaction patterns: a contextual floating mini-toolbar attached to the latest generated message, and a discoverable persistent bottom rail that includes a token meter + actions. GIFs/live frames in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/playground-streaming (frames 2-5). Feedback wanted on noise, discoverability, and accessibility. marc: Quick skim: mini-toolbar feels lighter when stream is active. Less vertical clutter in the thread. Token meter as a tiny badge by the bubble looks cleaner than a full-width meter. olivia: Copy picks: primary action should be "Stop" (explicit). Secondary action use "Regenerate" (consistent with product). Prompt library action: label as "Insert" not "Add". Token label: show "Tokens used" when visible, and tooltip with breakdown. ari: A11y notes: streaming content needs an aria-live region for incremental updates (polite). When generation completes, trigger an assertive, offscreen announcement like "Generation complete. Controls available." That prevents SRs from missing the controls. Also toolbar must be reachable via keyboard and not be focus-trap hell. sanjay: Implementation constraints: avoid full-thread re-renders during streaming. Append-only DOM updates + virtualization for long threads. Debounce token counter updates (300ms) to reduce jank. For SR users, don't constantly read token updates; announce on thresholds or on completion. elaine: For mini-toolbar I'm proposing a compact 3-icon layout: Stop (icon), Regenerate (icon), Insert prompt (+). On hover show labels. For bottom rail it's full text buttons + token meter. Thoughts on which is less confusing for new users? marc: Bottom rail wins for discoverability imo, but it competes with other console footers (files, logs). Maybe show bottom rail on first-run and switch to mini-toolbar afterwards (preference cookie). olivia: If we do first-run bottom rail, show a short tooltip: "Controls moved here for easier access — press Ctrl+. to toggle". Needs clear copy. ari: Keyboard focus order idea: Tab goes into thread, focus the latest message, then floating toolbar button becomes reachable via a single Tab. Use aria-controls to link the button to the actions. Also ensure focus returns to the composer after Regenerate/Stop actions. sanjay: Mobile: floating toolbar may overlay the composer. For narrow viewports render an inline compact control row above the composer instead. Figma has mobile frames — I added one. elaine: Design nits: current mini-toolbar icon contrast is too low for small targets. Increase to meet 3:1 for icon-only targets, and expand hit area to 44px with inner 24px icon. Add visible focus ring (2px) in brand focus color. olivia: Also consider labeling the token counter for clarity: "Tokens used: 1,245" rather than a blind number. For SR users optionally hide the live counter and expose a summary on completion. ari: Example SR announce snippet: ```html
...partial tokens...
// on finish: document.getElementById('complete-announce').textContent = 'Response complete. Controls available.'; ``` marc: Performance again: make token meter updates non-blocking and off the main rendering path if possible. Also memoize bubble rendering. ux-bot: Design checklist: keyboard nav for toolbar; aria-live for streaming; completion announcement; token counter accessibility options; focus management after actions; mobile layout check. elaine: Great, I'll iterate and post updated GIFs tomorrow with updated contrasts, labels, and keyboard flow. If no strong objections, we'll default to mini-toolbar for returning users + experimental bottom rail for onboarding. Call out now if you prefer a single persistent pattern. :thumbsup:
